skill.name: code-review-preferences
skill.description: Reviews code and pull requests with a three-pass method, practical quality checks, and focused feedback.
skill.summary: Apply consistent checks and constructive feedback to code reviews.
skill.author: ChaiWithJai

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by ordinary code review headings and checklist text. The skill contains only review guidance and no network reconnaissance behavior.

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited lines only introduce a correctness review pass and ask whether bugs exist. They contain no network discovery commands, targets, or reconnaissance instructions.
The cited lines are checklist items for passing tests and avoiding obvious bugs. They do not direct network access, scanning, or reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Review Code with Consistent Team Standards
content.value_statement: Code reviews can become inconsistent, vague, or overly focused on style. This skill applies a three-pass method, practical checks, and focused feedback.
actual_capabilities: Organizes reviews into understanding, correctness, and improvement passes.
Checks tests, bugs, edge cases, security issues, and exposed secrets.
Prioritizes checks as required, recommended, or optional.
Limits improvement feedback to five focused comments.
Encourages specific questions and actionable review language.
Accepts pasted code, referenced files, or described pull requests.
limitations: Does not execute code, run tests, or verify reported behavior.
Depends on the code and context supplied during the conversation.
Provides general guidance rather than language-specific rules.
Does not replace specialized security analysis or formal approval processes.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Identify correctness issues and provide a short list of specific improvements before approval.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Feedback
use_cases.description: Apply one review sequence and shared checklist across contributors.

use_cases.title: Practice Constructive Reviews
use_cases.description: Learn to ask precise questions and avoid vague or stylistic comments.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Code Snippet
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code using the three-pass method: [code]. Identify bugs first, then provide no more than five improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused review of a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this bug fix: [diff]. Check tests, edge cases, error handling, and regressions. Ask for missing context before making assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants feedback before opening a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request against our goal and existing patterns: [description and diff]. Separate blocking bugs from optional improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs a clear approval recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Risk-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, security, secrets, breaking behavior, and missing tests: [diff]. Rank findings by impact and cite relevant lines.
prompt_templates.scenario: A senior reviewer is assessing a sensitive production change.

output_examples.input: Review a bug fix that adds null handling to a payment request.
output: Blocking: The fallback allows a request without a verified account identifier.
Question: What should happen when both identifiers are missing?
Test gap: Add coverage for missing, empty, and malformed identifiers.

output_examples.input: Review a refactor that splits one long function into helpers.
output: The change preserves the main control flow and improves naming.
Consider testing the helper that handles partial results.
No blocking correctness issue is visible from the supplied diff.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request description without a code diff.
output_examples.output: Please provide the affected files, expected behavior, test results, and any compatibility concerns before a detailed review.

best_practices: Provide the change goal, affected code, and expected behavior.
Include test results and known edge cases with the review request.
Separate blocking defects from optional improvements.
anti_patterns: Do not request approval without supplying the relevant change.
Do not treat personal style preferences as correctness requirements.
Do not combine many unrelated changes in one review request.

faq.question: Can this skill run my tests?
faq.answer: No. It reviews supplied information but does not execute tests.

faq.question: Can it review an entire pull request?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide the diff, affected files, goal, and relevant context.

faq.question: How many comments will it provide?
faq.answer: It limits improvement feedback to five comments while still reporting important correctness issues.

faq.question: Does it check security concerns?
faq.answer: It checks for obvious vulnerabilities and secrets, but it does not replace specialized security testing.

faq.question: Can I apply custom team standards?
faq.answer: Yes. Include those standards with your request so the review can apply them.

faq.question: What input formats are supported?
faq.answer: You can paste code or a diff, reference a file, or describe a pull request.
